definitions.explanation: A colloquial, non-technical term for harmful microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, and other pathogens. Used in everyday conversation, especially when talking about hygiene and illness.

examples.japanese: ばい{菌|きん}が{入|はい}らないように{手|て}を{洗|あら}おう。
examples.english: Let's wash our hands so germs don't get in.

examples.japanese: {傷口|きずぐち}からばい{菌|きん}が{入|はい}ると{化膿|かのう}する。
examples.english: If germs get into a wound, it will become infected.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}、{汚|きたな}いものを{触|さわ}ると「ばい{菌|きん}がつくよ」と{言|い}われたものだ。
examples.english: When I was a child, if I touched dirty things, people would say 'you'll get germs.'

notes:
USAGE:
An everyday word used particularly by and when speaking to children. Not a scientific term — in technical contexts, {細菌|さいきん} (bacteria), ウイルス (virus), or {微生物|びせいぶつ} (microorganism) are used instead.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ばい{菌|きん}が{入|はい}る (germs get in)
- ばい{菌|きん}がつく (germs stick to, germs spread)
- ばい{菌|きん}を{殺|ころ}す (to kill germs)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {細菌|さいきん}: bacteria — the technical/scientific term
- {病原菌|びょうげんきん}: pathogenic bacteria — medical term
- {雑菌|ざっきん}: miscellaneous bacteria — technical, used for non-specific contamination
